newsitem.title: CANADA: Foothills Pipe seeks support for new expansion.
newsitem.headline: Foothills Pipe seeks support for new expansion.

text.p: Foothills Pipe Lines Ltd said on Monday it would seek shipper support for an expansion of its Eastern Leg system, which carries gas to the Canada-U.S. border at Monchy, Saskatchewan from Alberta.

Foothills, co-owned by NOVA Corp and Westcoast Energy Inc, said the open season would offer prospective shippers the opportunity to boost firm export capacity further on the Saskatchewan segment of the pipeline starting in November 2000.

Foothills was already starting an expansion of its system by 700 million cubic feet per day by November 1998 to meet an corresponding expansion of the Northern Border Partners pipeline in the United States.
The company said the open season for the proposal, dubbed Expansion 2000, represented "the next logical, cost-effective step in expanding the Foothills pipeline system to the Midwest markets."
Potential shippers on Expansion 2000 were also invited to show interest in later capacity additions, to start as early as 2001.
Foothills said prospective shippers could submit bids for capacity during the open season, which was to run from February 25 to April 25, 1997.
The company would then determine the facilities it would require following an evaluation of bids. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
